senses.gloss:
श्नथ् श्नथ्, cl. 1. P. श्नथति (2nd sing.
Impv. Ved. श्नथिहि), शश्नाथ, अश्न-
थीत् (श्नथिष्टम्, ‘you two have destroyed,’ Ṛg-
veda VII. 99, 5), श्नथितुम्, Ved. to strike, injure,
hurt, destroy, slay, kill: Caus. श्नथयति, -यितुम्,
Aor. अशिश्नथत् (अशिश्नत् = हिनस्ति, Ṛg-veda VII.
28, 3), to do violence, kill; Desid. शिश्नथिषति:
Intens. शाश्नथ्यते, शाश्नत्ति; [cf. Goth. snithan,
‘to cut;’ Old Germ. snîdu; Angl. Sax. snidhan;
Hib. slethe, ‘cutting, striking.’]

श्नथयत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, Ved. injuring, destroy-
ing, destructive.
श्नथित, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. hurt, wounded.

श्नथितृ, ता, त्री, तृ, Ved. one who slays or
kills, a smiter; killing, destroying, destructive, deadly,
fatal.

श्नम् श्नम्, (in grammar) a technical term
for the verbal affix न, the characteristic sign of the
seventh class of roots.

श्ना श्ना, (in grammar) a technical term for
the affix ना, the characteristic sign of the ninth class
of roots.

स्ना स्ना (probably connected with rt.
1. स्नु), cl. 2. P. (ep. also A.) स्नाति (-ते),
Pot. P. स्नायात् (Manu IV. 82; A. anomalous, स्ना-
यीत, Mahā-bh. Vana-p. 7072), सस्नौ, स्नास्यति,
अस्नासीत्, Prec. स्नायात् or स्नेयात्, स्नातुम् (perhaps
originally ‘to float or swim,’ cf. rt. 1. स्नु, 3. नौ,
p. 518), to bathe, perform ablution; to perform the
ceremony of bathing when leaving the house of a
spiritual preceptor: Caus. स्नापयति or स्नप-
यति (with preps. the form स्नापयति is more
correct), to cause to bathe, wash, cleanse, bathe,
wet; to bathe with tears, weep for (?): Desid. सि-
स्नासति: Intens. सास्नायते, सास्नाति, सास्नेति; [cf.
Gr. νά-ω, νᾶ-μα, να-ρό-ς, νη-ρό-ς, νῆ-αο-ς, νίπτω,
νή-χ-ω for ανή-χ-ω; Lat. nâ-re, nâ-s (= Sans. स्नासि),
na-ta-re, na-su-s; Goth. nadr; Angl. Sax. nœd-
dre, nedre; Old Germ. nacho; Hib. snamhaim,
‘I swim.’]
स्नपन स्नपन, स्नपित. See below.

स्नपन, अस्, आ, अम्, causing to bathe; used for
bathing (as water &c.); (अम्), n. causing to bathe,
bathing, ablution; washing, sprinkling, wetting.

स्नापन, अम्, n. the act of causing to bathe or
attending a person while bathing, (Manu II. 209.)
—स्नापनोच्छिष्ट-भोजन (˚न-उच्˚), ए, n. du.
the act of bathing another person and eating his
leavings, (Manu II. 209.)
स्नव स्नव. See under rt. 1. स्नु.
स्नव, अस्, m. oozing, drizzling, dripping, trickling.

स्नाव, अस्, m. (the form स्नावानि, neut. pl., occurs),
a tendon, muscle; (according to some) the vascular
membrane investing the bones; [cf. probably Old
Germ. senwa; Angl. Sax. sinu, sinw, senw.]

स्नस् स्नस्, cl. 1. 4. P. स्नसति, स्नस्यति,
सस्नास, &c., (according to some) to
eject, eject from the mouth, reject (निरासे); to
inhabit (निवासे, according to others); to eat (?); [cf.
rt. स्नुस्]: Caus. स्नसयति or स्नासयति, &c.

स्नपित, अस्, आ, अम्, bathed, washed, sprinkled,
wetted, moistened.

स्नापित, अस्, आ, अम्, caused to bathe, attended on
while bathing, immersed.

स्नात्, आन्, आती or आन्ती, आत्, bathing, performing
ablution.

स्नात, अस्, आ, अम्, bathed, washed, purified by ab-
lution, pure; (अस्), m. one whose spiritual instruc-
tion is finished; an initiated householder.
—स्नाता-
नुलिप्त (˚त-अन्˚), अस्, आ, अम्, one who is both bathed
and anointed.

स्नातक, अस्, m. a Brāhman who has performed
the ceremony of ablution (cf. आ-प्लव) required on
his finishing his first Āśrama or period of studentship
as a Brahma-cārin (and on becoming initiated into
the second Āśrama or order of a Gṛha-stha, q. v.);
a Brāhman just returned from the house of his pre-
ceptor and become a married man or initiated house-
holder, (three kinds of Snātakas are enumerated,
1. the Vidyā-snātaka or Brahma-cārin, who, at the
end of his period of studentship, has completed a
course of study of the Vedas only; 2. the Vrata-
snātaka, who has completed the prescribed Vratas or
vowed observances, such as fasting, continence, &c.,
without becoming perfect in the Vedas; 3. the Vidyā-
vrata-snātaka or Ubhaya-snātaka, who has com-
pleted both the Vedas and the Vratas; this last is of
course regarded as the highest kind, see Kullūka on
Manu III. 2); a Brāhman who is a Bhikṣu or
asker of alms for any religious object or legitimate
purpose, (nine kinds are enumerated in Manu XI. 1);
any man of the first three classes who is an initiated
householder.

स्नातृ, ता, त्री, तृ, one who bathes or washes, a
bather.

स्नात्व, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. fit for ablutions, capable
of being used for bathing, (Sāy. स्नात्वाः = स्नानार्-
हाः, Ṛg-veda X. 71, 7.)

स्नात्वा (Ved. also स्नात्वी), ind. having bathed or
washed, having performed ablutions.

स्नान, अम्, n. bathing, washing, ablution, dipping
in water, wetting, purification by bathing, religious
or ceremonial ablution, bathing in sacred waters
(considered as a daily observance or as an essential
part of some ceremonial); the ceremony of bathing
or anointing an idol; anything used in ablution (e. g.
water, perfumed powder for the body, &c.).
—स्ना-
न-तृण, अम्, n. ‘bathing-grass,’ Kuśa grass.
—स्ना-
न-दीपिका, f., N. of a commentary by Gopī-nātha
on the Snāna-sūtra.
—स्नान-द्रोणी, f. a bathing-tub.
—स्नान-यात्रा, f. ‘bathing procession,’ the festival
held on the day of full moon in the month Jyeṣṭha
(when images of Kṛṣṇa as Jagan-nātha are carried
out and bathed; in Orissa this festival is called
Ratha-yātrā).
—स्नानयात्रिक, अस्, आ, अम्, attend-
ing the above procession at the bathing of Jagan-
nātha.
—स्नान-वस्त्र, अम्, n. a cloth put on for
bathing, a bathing-dress, wet cloth.
—स्नान-विधि, इस्,
m. the rules of ablution, proper manner of bathing;
N. of a Pariśiṣṭa of the Sāma-veda.
—स्नान-शील,
अस्, आ, अम्, fond of bathing, observing or performing
ablution (especially in sacred waters).
—स्नान-सूत्र,
अम्, n., N. of a Sūtra work (ascribed to Kātyāyana).
—स्नानसूत्र-पद्धति, इस्, f., N. of a summary
of a commentary by Hari-jīvana-miśra on the Snāna-
sūtra.
—स्नानागार (˚न-आग्˚), अम्, n. a bath-room.
—स्नानोत्तीर्ण (˚न-उत्˚), अस्, आ, अम्, rising up from
a bath, one who has just completed his ablutions.

स्नानीय, अस्, आ, अम्, fit for bathing or ablution,
suitable for bathing; (अम्), n. water or any article
(such as unguents, perfumed powders, &c.) proper
for bathing.
—स्नानीय-वस्त्र, अम्, n. a cloth tied
round the waist for bathing, a bathing dress.

स्नापक, अस्, m. (fr. the Caus.), a servant who
bathes his master or attends him while bathing
(bringing water and pouring it over his person).

स्नायिन्, ई, इनी, इ, bathing; (ई), m. a bather, per-
former of ablutions.

स्नास्यत्, अन्, अती or अन्ती, अत्, about to bathe or
perform an initiatory ceremonial ablution; (अन्), m.
a religious student about to become a Snātaka, (Manu
II. 245.)

स्नायु स्नायु, उस्, f. (according to some उस्,
m.; said in Uṇādi-s. I. 1. to be fr. rt. स्ना), a sinew,
tendon, muscle (described as वायु-वाहिनी-नाडी, ‘a
tubular vessel conveying vital air’); the string of a
bow; [cf. probably Gr. νεῦρο-ν, νευρ-ά; Lat. ner-
vu-s, nerviœ, nervosus; Old Germ. snar-a, snar-
ahha, snuor, narwa; Old Sax. naru; Lith. nar-
a-s, ner-u.]
—स्नायु-बन्धन, अम्, n. a sinew-
string.
—स्नायु-मय, अस्, ई, अम्, made of tendons.
—स्नायु-युत, अस्, आ, अम्, possessed of tendons,
(Manu VI. 76.)
—स्नायु-रज्जु, उस्, उस्, उ, having
tendons for cords (said of the body).
—स्नाय्व्-अर्मन्,
अ, n. a kind of disease of the eyes.
स्नायुक = स्नायु above.

स्नावन्, आ, m. (according to Uṇādi-s. IV. 112. fr.
rt. स्ना), a muscle, sinew (Ved.); = रसिक, a
lover (?).

स्नवन, अम्, n. the act of oozing, trickling;
distillation.
